summary: Reviewed the 15:26Z Seed-B uploads and continued static analysis. The latest runtime seed/address pair is 5B4AE67D9C2A8F61 / 0001BF0004E84EFD. Fresh caller extraction ties the session to NMS.exe SHA-256 671de22649274b49fa07f5a246bc7252c4e08bb9ab623d2e65722fbab4e497a4; its caller window matches the live exact-root bytes. Disassembly of the hash-matched uploaded caller windows narrows the flow: function candidate 006388A0 reads the descriptor primary seed at object+0x138 (descriptor at +0x128) and use_seed at +0x140. Calls at 006377B6 and 00637D86 pass an object through as the second argument. In the 00637660 wrapper path, an incoming stack argument is forwarded through helper 00637DB0 and initializer 006377E0, which copies/initializes the embedded descriptor at +0x128 via call 00227A40. This is direct byte/argument-flow evidence that seed source is supplied upstream of 00637660; it is not evidence of how that value was generated. The available windows do not include callers or vtable slots for 00637660, so the universe-address-to-root-seed derivation remains unproven. A read-only static reference scanner is now committed on this lane at agent-patches/seed-lineage/seed_b_trace_static_callers.py (commit 6243812f4e7b94c75f0d6055055c2fdd947e7f76; SHA-256 7fa2dca6a6ab02caec5601b9549cf1d352da78dbc4539cb12d3c2e12255f4d20). It was syntax-checked and tested against a synthetic PE fixture for both a direct rel32 call and an absolute pointer slot. The scan's 325-byte windows place each reference exactly at offset 160, so they omit the preceding function setup and do not show enough of the caller to identify source-object initialization. The matching NMS.exe is not present in the shared workspace. Existing lane tooling can extract bounded RVA windows locally without launching NMS. An additional offline export around the three caller sites is now the only blocker; no game traversal, probe restart, or controller capture is required. User attached NMS(1).exe, which is byte-identified by SHA-256 671de22649274b49fa07f5a246bc7252c4e08bb9ab623d2e65722fbab4e497a4. I parsed its PE .pdata function table and disassembled full caller/helper ranges. Measured flow: incoming R9 to 00637660 is passed unchanged to 00637DB0, preserved as R14, then passed as the first stack argument to 006377E0; 006377E0 forwards it to 00227A40, which copies/initializes the embedded descriptor at destination object+0x128. The three direct callers supply local records at [rbp-0x20], [rbp-0x28], and [rbp-0x38]. This locates the descriptor source argument but does not link these static paths to the live root event or establish a universe-address-to-seed transform. Continued offline analysis of the supplied matching executable. The object-creation path carries the 00637660 incoming R9 descriptor through 00637DB0/006377E0 and copies it at 00227A40; the generated-object consumer path at 006388A0 falls through into adjacent .pdata code at 006388F9, which reads object+0x138 and tests +0x140. One direct caller, 001B2CF9, fills that descriptor field through an invertible 64-bit mixer of a sign-extended 32-bit global state value. Inverting the mixer for the three known root-seed candidates gives no sign-extended 32-bit input, so this path cannot directly emit those candidates if the observed copy path is unchanged. The other two callers (02D042E1, 02D04AF8) remain under investigation. Added exact .pdata caller bounds to the scanner; 2/2 focused tests and py_compile passed. No new game run or traversal is needed while the static trace continues.
